source_signature.notes: Space trusses — three-dimensional joint and member equilibrium, authored to the Architect scope ruling that the distinguishing feature be genuinely three-dimensional and not a re-run of the planar method of joints. Independently re-derived: |r_AD| = sqrt(4 + 9 + 36) = sqrt(49) = 7 m, u_AD = (2/7, 3/7, 6/7) with all three components nonzero and normalization (4 + 9 + 36)/49 = 1, so member AD has a genuinely three-dimensional line of action rather than a coordinate-aligned one. The joint solves by THREE scalar equations: from sum Fz, F_AD = 7(7/6) = 49/6 = 8.1667 kN tension; from sum Fy, F_AC = -(49/6)(3/7) = -3.5 kN compression; from sum Fx, F_AB = -(49/6)(2/7) = -7/3 = -2.3333 kN compression. Verified by an independent z-balance, F_AD(6/7) = 49/7 = 7 kN balancing the applied load without reference to the x or y equations, and by sign reading consistent with a downward load putting AD in tension while AB and AC resist. THE DISTINGUISHING FEATURE BITES: the third equation carries real work because the member with the only z-component isolates from sum Fz, so the resolution genuinely exercises three-dimensional direction cosines and cannot be a planar problem wearing a z-axis; the artifact states explicitly that a planar two-equation resolution is insufficient and sum Fz is not optional, and states the space-truss determinacy relation m + r = 3j contrasted with the planar m + r = 2j. BOUNDARY against the signed plane-truss family: method_of_joints owns the planar two-equation joint and its complement is named in one sentence; simple_truss_modeling's planar idealization is cited as the analogue with ball-and-socket joints replacing pins and not re-authored; zero_force_members and method_of_sections are excluded; the 3D unit-vector and force-along-line mechanics of unit_vector_along_line and force_directed_along_line are cited and not re-derived. No mass, no dynamics. SYMBOL DISCIPLINE, with one sharp catch: cartesian_vector_components_3d binds k as the +z unit vector, and this artifact uses sum Fz and z-components throughout without ever binding a bare k, avoiding the collision rather than stumbling into it; F_AB, F_AC, F_AD reused tension-positive from method_of_joints, the unit-vector framing reused from unit_vector_along_line, and m, r, j reused as counts from simple_truss_modeling; no binding of d, k, I, M_O, theta, A_gen or V. Three earned signals at distinct steps: sign_or_placement_error at step 2 where each unit vector is formed from the joint outward and the tension-positive convention is set, covering unit-vector reversal and wrong force sense; axis_confusion at step 3 where the three scalar equations are assembled, covering applying only two equations, dropping sum Fz, and Cartesian component mismatch; and unclassified at step 1 as the boundary fallback covering re-running the planar method as the objective and using 2j determinacy. simple_average_used cannot be earned. solution_sequencing_error omitted and argued: solving sum Fz first is convenient algebra on a simultaneous set of three equations all available at once, not a forced phase order stranding a prerequisite — the correct distinction from general_analysis_procedure, where the phases genuinely could not proceed out of order. Honest limitation recorded: the single-joint solution with three unknowns and three equations determines these member forces but does not verify global determinacy or proper constraint, owned by the determinacy and constraint skills; a negative scalar means compression, not an error; and the normalization check confirms u_AD is a unit vector but does not validate the given joint coordinates. First skill authored in the newly created SPACE_TRUSSES subtopic; signed from that re-parented location; required no correction at review.
